title: A sheaf of sets on a space with a basis of quasi-compact opens is a directed colimit of finitely presented sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal B$ a basis of the topology of $X$ such that every $U\in\mathcal B$ is quasi-compact. For an open $U\subseteq X$ and a set $S$ let $j_{U!}\underline S$ be the extension by the empty set [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty] of the sheaf $\underline S_U$ of locally constant maps to $S$ on $U$. Coproducts and coequalizers below are colimits in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of sets on $X$. Then there are a directed set $\Lambda$ (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), a system of sheaves of sets $(\mathcal F_\lambda,\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:\mathcal F_\lambda\to\mathcal F_\mu)_{\lambda\le\mu}$ on $X$ over $\Lambda$ ($\varphi_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{\nu\mu}\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\varphi_{\nu\lambda}$) and morphisms $c_\lambda:\mathcal F_\lambda\to\mathcal F$ with $c_\mu\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=c_\lambda$, such that $(\mathcal F,(c_\lambda)_\lambda)$ is a colimit of the system in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$, and such that for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ there are integers $m,n\ge0$, elements $U_1,\dots,U_n,V_1,\dots,V_m\in\mathcal B$, finite sets $S_1,\dots,S_n,T_1,\dots,T_m$, two morphisms $\beta,\gamma:\coprod_{b=1}^mj_{V_b!}\underline{T_b}\to\coprod_{a=1}^nj_{U_a!}\underline{S_a}$ and a morphism $q:\coprod_{a=1}^nj_{U_a!}\underline{S_a}\to\mathcal F_\lambda$ such that $(\mathcal F_\lambda,q)$ is a coequalizer of $\beta,\gamma$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (basis-generated epimorphism).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-basis-surjection] to obtain an epimorphism $p:\mathcal F_0=\coprod_{a\in A}j_{U_a!}\underline{S_a}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F$, with each $U_a$ in the basis and each $S_a$ finite. The construction in Tag 0CAH chooses a basis neighbourhood for every germ of $\mathcal F$ and uses the adjunction and stalk description of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty-adjunction] to prove surjectivity on stalks.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAH (lemma-surjection), line 2992 and proof

proof.text: *Step 2 (the relation presentation).* Form the kernel pair $K=\mathcal F_0\times_{\mathcal F}\mathcal F_0$ of $p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-basis-surjection] to $K$ and write the resulting epimorphism as $e:\coprod_{b\in B}j_{V_b!}\underline{T_b}\twoheadrightarrow K$, with $V_b$ in the basis and $T_b$ finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-surjection-kernel-pair-coequalizer], composing $e$ with the two projections of $K$ gives maps $r,s:\coprod_{b\in B}j_{V_b!}\underline{T_b}\rightrightarrows\coprod_{a\in A}j_{U_a!}\underline{S_a}$ whose coequalizer is $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAI (lemma-filtered-colimit-constructibles), proof at lines 3038-3046

proof.text: *Step 3 (finite support of the relation maps).* For a finite subset $B'\subset B$, each of the two maps from $\coprod_{b\in B'}j_{V_b!}\underline{T_b}$ into the right-hand coproduct factors through a finite subcoproduct indexed by some finite $A'\subset A$. Indeed, the value on each quasi-compact $V_b$ commutes with the directed colimit expressing the infinite coproduct, by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-directed-colimit-sections]; the factorization for both maps is obtained by taking the union of their finite supports. Thus the relation data has finite truncations.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAI (lemma-filtered-colimit-constructibles), proof at lines 3047-3058

proof.text: *Step 4 (directed colimit of finite coequalizers).* Let $\Lambda$ be the directed set of finite relation truncations, ordered by inclusion and enlargement of the finite supports in $A$. For $\lambda=(B',A')$, let $\mathcal F_\lambda$ be the coequalizer of the two restricted maps between the corresponding finite coproducts. Enlarging supports gives transition maps, and the canonical cocone to the coequalizer $\mathcal F$ is compatible. The finite-support assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-finite-relation-truncations] shows that every relation in the infinite presentation appears at some stage; hence the induced map from the colimit of the $\mathcal F_\lambda$ to $\mathcal F$ is both locally surjective and locally injective, so is an isomorphism of sheaves. Therefore $\mathcal F$ is the directed colimit of the stated finite coequalizers.
